question.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{5x}$ at $x=e.$
question.worked_solution:
The slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=e$ equals the function's derivative at the corresponding point.

We have the function 

$$
y=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{5x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{5x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =5x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(5x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x))+(5x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =5\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+5x\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{x}) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\frac{5}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =5(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(5(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}))\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{5x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =5(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{5x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of $y=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{5x}$ at $x=e$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}{|}_{x=e} & =5(\operatorname{ln}⁡e)^{5\cdot e}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡e)+\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡e}) \\  & =5(1)^{5e}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+\frac{1}{1}) \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
